home.name: binbin
home.intro: Since June 2025 I've been working on an AI nail platform and a multi-tenant HRIS at Manience Inc. Outside work, I independently built and now run two systems in daily use at NKUST. This site records how these systems were designed — the trade-offs made and the lessons learned — in the form of engineering notes.

about.title: About
about.p1: I'm binbin — still a student, and since June 2025 a full-stack developer at Manience Inc., where I build the AI nail platform and the dozens of Django microservices behind it.
about.p2: During acceptance on the HR system I found that the payroll API cached without the user in the key — inside one TTL window an employee would hit an admin’s cached response and see company-wide salaries. It threw no error, it was not slow, the tests were green. That is when I started believing that cache design is authorization design.

deck.evidenceTitle: Every number traces back to source
deck.evidenceNote: Each figure comes from a repo of mine, and every case study states its source and the system's status at the time — including what did not pass acceptance.
deck.fact1Note: Multi-tenant HR SaaS acceptance, 87.5% pass rate
deck.fact2Note: SEC-001–030 on the alumni platform, all closed before launch
deck.fact3Note: Equipment lending system, green on a single VPS
deck.fact4Note: Plus 2,271 failures, all one empty-field root cause
deck.systemsTitle: Each one opens into a full breakdown
deck.sys1Note: 36 modules, 728 endpoints; isolation pushed into the base layer. Company-internal, in acceptance.
deck.sys2Note: Flipped AllowAny to default-deny and closed SEC-001–030 before launch. Live on the university domain.
deck.sys3Note: I used the old one as a student worker, so I knew what to build. 1,112 tests.
deck.sys4Note: Started as an industry-academia project — ~80% of the backend, ~40% of the frontend; stayed on after the warranty period.
deck.pathTitle: One thing led to the next
deck.tl1Note: A food-surplus marketplace; wrote the system at CDRI and presented on their behalf at DIGI⁺Talent.
deck.tl2Note: Picked up server duty then — Ubuntu, web servers, VMs — and still run them.
deck.tl3Note: Museum × Ministry of Education AI health program; Django backend, React frontend, entity-tagging model.
deck.tl4: Industry projects and the alumni platform
deck.tl4Note: Two industry-academia projects at once, plus the alumni platform handed to me by a professor.
deck.tl5Note: Stayed on after the warranty period; HR SaaS, ops console and the app frontend.
